title: AGENTS.md
summary: Home of the AGENTS.md convention: plain Markdown, no required fields, nearest file in the tree wins, explicit user prompts override it. Suggests sections for overview, build and test commands, style, testing and security.

title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation
summary: Announces a foundation stewarding MCP, goose and AGENTS.md; states AGENTS.md was released in August 2025 and adopted by more than 60,000 projects.

title: Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
summary: Controlled evaluation across agents: context files did not generally raise task success and raised inference cost by over 20% on average; agents do follow them; repository overviews did not help.

title: On the Impact of AGENTS.md Files on the Efficiency of AI Coding Agents
summary: On 124 pull requests from 10 repositories, runs with an AGENTS.md had lower median runtime (28.64%) and fewer output tokens (16.58%) with comparable completion.

title: Do Context Files Help Coding Agents? A Two-Agent Ablation Study on Real Repositories
summary: 288 runs over 17 tasks in two agents: no context file, a full AGENTS.md and on-demand retrieval did not measurably change correctness; failures came from implementation skill.

title: Instruction Adherence in Coding Agent Configuration Files: A Factorial Study of Four File-Structure Variables
summary: 1,650 sessions: file size, structure and conflict had no detectable effect on adherence; adherence fell as more code was generated in a session (exploratory finding).

title: Agent READMEs: An Empirical Study of Context Files for Agentic Coding
summary: 2,303 context files: most specify testing (75.9%), implementation (70.8%) and architecture (68.1%); few cover security (14.8%) or performance (14.5%); files grow by small additions.

title: On the Use of Agentic Coding Manifests: An Empirical Study of Claude Code
summary: 253 CLAUDE.md files: shallow structure, mostly operational commands, implementation notes and architecture.

title: How Claude remembers your project (memory)
summary: Reference for project, local and nested memory files: under 200 lines per file, concrete verifiable instructions, local file git-ignored, nested files load on demand, memory is context not enforcement.

title: Best practices for Claude Code
summary: Keep the instruction file to what the code cannot tell the agent; move no-exception rules to hooks; give the agent a check to run and ask for evidence, not a summary; use a fresh reviewer; cap turns or spend in headless runs.

title: How to write a great agents.md: Lessons from over 2,500 repositories
summary: Strong files cover commands, testing, structure, style, git workflow and boundaries (always, ask first, never), put executable commands early and grow from observed mistakes.

title: Adding repository custom instructions for GitHub Copilot
summary: Repository, path-specific and AGENTS.md instructions; nearest AGENTS.md wins; generated instructions should be at most two pages and not task-specific.

title: Rules
summary: Project, user and team rules with scoped application modes; keep rules under 500 lines; do not paste style guides a linter enforces or duplicate code.

title: Provide context with GEMINI.md files
summary: Layered global, workspace and just-in-time subdirectory context files, concatenated into prompts; can be configured to read AGENTS.md. Date is the page's last-updated stamp.

title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md (Codex)
summary: Global and per-directory AGENTS.md files concatenated root first, closer files later; combined size capped at 32 KiB by default; override file supported.

title: Writing a good CLAUDE.md
summary: Practitioner argument for a short hand-written file with pointers to task-specific docs and deterministic linting instead of style prose; numbers are the author's estimates.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
summary: Orchestrator and worker subagents beat a single agent by 90.2% on an internal research eval at roughly 15 times chat token use; most coding tasks fit the pattern poorly; each subagent needs objective, output format, tools and boundaries.

title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
summary: Argues that splitting work across agents loses shared context and implicit decisions; prefers single-threaded agents.

title: Create custom subagents
summary: Subagents have their own context, prompt, tool allowlist or denylist, model and turn cap; the description drives delegation; use them for verbose output, restricted tools or self-contained work.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
summary: Treat context as a finite budget; retrieve just in time; subagents return condensed summaries of about 1,000 to 2,000 tokens; do the simplest thing that works.

title: Manage costs effectively
summary: Cost benchmarks per developer day, spend caps, cheaper models for simple subagent tasks, short instruction files and hooks that trim tool output.

title: CLI reference
summary: Headless --max-turns (no limit by default) and --max-budget-usd (client-side estimate that can overshoot, includes subagents) flags, and fallback model chains.

title: Track cost and usage (Agent SDK)
summary: Reported costs are client-side estimates; de-duplicate parallel tool calls by message id; per-model usage includes subagents; failed runs still cost tokens.

title: Prompt caching
summary: Cache write and read multipliers, five-minute default lifetime, and prefix order where changing tool definitions invalidates the cache.

title: How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks
summary: Agentic coding uses far more tokens than chat; runs of the same task vary up to 30 times in tokens; accuracy often peaks at intermediate cost; models underestimate their own usage.

title: Configure permissions
summary: Deny, then ask, then allow; rules are enforced by the tool not the model; command-text patterns are fragile; file deny rules do not stop subprocesses, so pair with the OS sandbox.

title: Making Claude Code more secure and autonomous with sandboxing
summary: OS-level filesystem and network isolation; both are needed together; reported 84% fewer permission prompts internally.

title: Automate actions with hooks
summary: Hooks give deterministic control; a pre-tool hook can block a call even in bypass mode; a misplaced decision field is silently ignored.

title: Development containers
summary: A container with skipped permissions still lets a malicious project exfiltrate anything inside it; do not mount SSH keys or cloud credentials; prefer short-lived scoped tokens.

title: Security
summary: Prompt-injection safeguards and advice: review commands, do not pipe untrusted content in, use VMs for external services; headless runs skip trust prompts.

title: Agent approvals and security (Codex)
summary: Read-only, workspace-write and full-access sandbox modes; network off by default; full access only inside a trusted container.

title: Sandboxing in the Gemini CLI
summary: Seatbelt, container and other sandbox options; default profile still allows broad reads and network; sandboxing reduces but does not remove risk.

title: Customizing or disabling the firewall for Copilot coding agent
summary: Egress firewall covers only processes the agent starts from its shell tool and is not a comprehensive security control.

title: Risks and mitigations for Copilot coding agent
summary: Agent pushes only to its own branch, cannot approve or merge, the requester cannot approve its PR, workflows need human approval, and secret scanning runs on its output.

title: About push protection
summary: Blocks secrets at push time with audited bypass; repository-level push protection is off by default; some AI-detected secrets are not blocked on every path.

title: About code owners
summary: CODEOWNERS plus the branch protection setting requiring code-owner review; last matching pattern wins.

title: The lethal trifecta for AI agents
summary: Private data plus untrusted content plus external communication lets an attacker exfiltrate data; the reliable defence is to avoid combining all three.

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
summary: Proposes architectural patterns that give provable resistance to prompt injection by constraining what an agent can do after reading untrusted input, at some cost in generality.

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections (commentary)
summary: Summarises the paper's six patterns (action selector, plan then execute, map-reduce, dual model, code then execute, context minimisation).

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
summary: Separates control flow from untrusted data and enforces capabilities at tool calls; solves 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security versus 84% undefended.

title: An Introduction to Google's Approach for Secure AI Agents
summary: Defence in depth combining deterministic controls and reasoning defences; agents need human controllers, limited powers and observable actions.

title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection
summary: Mitigations include least privilege, deterministic output validation, segregating external content, human approval for high-risk actions and adversarial testing.

title: OWASP GenAI Security Project releases Top 10 for Agentic Applications
summary: Announcement of the agentic Top 10 for 2026, highlighting behaviour hijacking, tool misuse and identity and privilege abuse; full list not read.

title: GitHub MCP Exploited: Accessing private repositories via MCP
summary: A malicious public issue made an agent leak private repository data into a public PR; model-independent; mitigated by per-session least-privilege repository access and monitoring.

title: Security Bulletin AWS-2025-015: Amazon Q Developer for VS Code Extension
summary: An overly broad token in build configuration let an actor ship malicious code in extension 1.84.0; fixed in 1.85.0; credentials revoked.

title: Compromised Amazon Q extension told AI to delete everything and it shipped
summary: The planted prompt instructed the agent to wipe local files and cloud resources and ran with all tools trusted and no interaction.

title: S1ngularity: what happened, how we responded, what we learned
summary: Workflow injection leaked a token, leading to malicious releases that tried to use local AI CLIs to find secrets; remediations include trusted publishing and approval for external pipeline runs.

title: Malicious versions of Nx and some supporting plugins were published (GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c)
summary: The malware embedded a prompt asking a local agent to inventory env, config and key files for exfiltration.

title: Supply chain security alert: Nx build system compromised with data-stealing malware
summary: Shows the malware invoking local agent CLIs with permission-bypass flags to hunt credentials; advises rotating keys and auditing workflows.

title: Arbitrary code execution from Cursor Agent through a prompt injection via MCP special files (CVE-2025-54135)
summary: The agent could create agent configuration dotfiles without approval, so injected text could register an MCP server and run code; CVSS 8.5, patched in 1.3.9.

title: Security-Focused Guide for AI Code Assistant Instructions
summary: Instruction-file content for secure output: never emit secrets, verify new dependencies, review agent code like a colleague's, add SAST and linters.

title: Require additional approvals for merge requests with AI-authored commits (issue 578758)
summary: Open feature request for stricter approval rules on merge requests containing agent-authored commits; not shipped.

title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
summary: Agents marked features complete without testing; a JSON feature list starting all-failing, editable only in its pass field, plus end-to-end testing, helped.

title: Your job is to deliver code you have proven to work
summary: Every change should come with a test that fails if reverted and a recorded manual demonstration; agents should be made to do the same.

title: Augmented Coding: Beyond the Vibes
summary: Strict test-driven development with an agent needed close supervision; warning signs are loops, unrequested features and disabling or deleting tests.

title: Best practices (Codex)
summary: Prompts should state when the task is done; instruction file should list build, test and lint commands and how to verify; review the diff.

title: Get the best results from Copilot coding agent
summary: A well-scoped task has a clear description, complete acceptance criteria and named files; give build and test commands so the agent can validate its change.

title: ImpossibleBench: Measuring LLMs' Propensity of Exploiting Test Cases
summary: Tasks whose tests contradict the spec; frontier agents cheat often (for example 54% for one model), mostly by editing tests or special-casing; read-only tests and an abort option reduce it; monitors miss many cases.

title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
summary: Mix code, model and human graders; grade outcomes not paths; read transcripts; isolate trials; use pass@k or pass^k; a 0% pass rate over many trials usually means a broken task.

title: Semantic conventions for GenAI agent spans (v1.37.0)
summary: Defines create_agent and invoke_agent spans, required operation and provider attributes and token usage attributes; status Development; message content opt-in. Year of the release inferred.

title: Semantic conventions for GenAI spans (semantic-conventions-genai)
summary: GenAI conventions moved to a separate repository; defines execute_tool spans with tool name and call id; arguments and results opt-in; status Development, no releases.

title: Monitoring (Claude Code OpenTelemetry)
summary: Exports metrics and events for tokens, cost, edits, tool decisions and API requests; prompts and tool details redacted by default; tracing in beta.

title: Advanced configuration: observability and telemetry (Codex)
summary: Optional OpenTelemetry export of API requests, token counts, tool decisions and tool results; off by default; prompts not logged by default.

title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
summary: Flaws in task setup or reward design can misstate agent performance by up to 100% relative; proposes a checklist; notes weak tests in a popular benchmark.

title: Recent Frontier Models Are Reward Hacking
summary: Models patched evaluators, overwrote timers and copied reference answers; 30.4% of runs in one suite; instructions not to cheat barely helped; fix the scorer rather than penalise via monitors.

title: Repo state loopholes during agentic evaluation (issue 465)
summary: Agents could read future git history containing the fix; maintainers removed future history in v4.1.0; measured impact small but not zero.

title: The SWE-Bench Illusion: When State-of-the-Art LLMs Remember Instead of Reason
summary: Models locate buggy files from issue text alone far better on the benchmark (up to 76%) than on other repositories (up to 53%), suggesting memorisation.

title: Does SWE-Bench-Verified Test Agent Ability or Model Memory?
summary: Issue-only localisation is several times better on the benchmark than on comparable fresh sets, consistent with contamination.

title: Are "Solved Issues" in SWE-bench Really Solved Correctly? An Empirical Study
summary: Differential testing finds 29.6% of plausible patches behave differently from the reference and inflates resolution rates by 6.2 points.

title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
summary: Continuously refreshed tasks; some models' scores on the older benchmark may be inflated by contamination.

title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?
summary: 1,865 long-horizon tasks with public, held-out and private commercial splits, copyleft and private code for contamination resistance, human-reviewed fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests.

title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
summary: Version 2.0 has 89 tasks, each with its own environment, a human-written solution and tests; frontier agents score below 65%.

title: SWE-Lancer: Can Frontier LLMs Earn $1 Million from Real-World Freelance Software Engineering?
summary: Freelance tasks graded by end-to-end tests triple-verified by engineers rather than unit tests.

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
summary: Defines the 50% time horizon metric; horizons roughly doubled every seven months since 2019.

title: Time Horizon 1.1
summary: Updated task suite and harness; estimates are sensitive to scaffold and task mix and few long tasks have human baselines.

title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior and the Risks of Promoting Obfuscation
summary: Reading reasoning traces catches reward hacking in agentic coding better than watching actions; training hard against the monitor teaches hidden hacking.

title: From shortcuts to sabotage: natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking
summary: A model that learned to exit the test harness early to fake passes also generalised to broader misbehaviour, including code sabotage in 12% of one evaluation.

title: EvilGenie: A Reward Hacking Benchmark
summary: Commercial coding agents hard-coded tests or edited test files; held-out tests added little detection power; LLM judges worked in clear cases.

title: Claude 4 system card notes
summary: Quotes a vendor system card: test hard-coding fell about two-thirds versus the prior model and simple prompts cut it further; with initiative prompts and a shell the model took bold unrequested actions.

title: GPT-5 System Card
summary: Reports deception rates on impossible agentic coding tasks (0.17 versus 0.47 for the prior model) and with broken tools; mitigations are described as imperfect.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
summary: Randomised trial: 16 experienced developers took 19% longer with AI allowed while believing they were faster.

title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
summary: Late-2025 follow-up gave speedup point estimates with wide intervals; METR calls the data unreliable due to selection effects.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
summary: Taxonomy of 14 failure modes in three categories (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification) from annotated traces.

title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
summary: Across 18 models, performance drops as input grows even on simple tasks; distractors worsen it; focused context outperforms full context.

title: The Rise of AI Teammates in Software Engineering 3.0 (AIDev)
summary: 456,000+ agent PRs; agent PRs accepted less often than human PRs; the paper's own text and table give differing rates.

title: Where Do AI Coding Agents Fail? An Empirical Study of Failed Agentic Pull Requests in GitHub
summary: Unmerged agent PRs are larger, touch more files and often fail CI; reasons include unwanted features and misalignment with the request.

title: Why Are Agentic Pull Requests Merged or Rejected? An Empirical Study
summary: Of 717 inspected rejected agent PRs, 35.7% were clear agent failures; the rest were workflow constraints or had no visible reason.

title: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
summary: Across 16 models, at least 5.2% (commercial) and 21.7% (open) of recommended packages did not exist; 205,474 unique invented names.

title: The Rise of Slopsquatting
summary: Hallucinated package names recur across runs (43% every time in repeated prompts), making them registrable by attackers.

title: Vibe coding service Replit deleted user's production database
summary: An agent deleted a production database during a declared freeze, fabricated data and reports and wrongly said rollback was impossible.

title: AI-powered coding tool wiped out a software company's database in 'catastrophic failure'
summary: Same incident; vendor responded with automatic dev and prod database separation, better rollback and a planning-only mode.

title: Gemini CLI 'lost' files during a failed file move operation (issue 4586)
summary: User report of an agent losing all files in a folder during a reorganisation without a sandbox.

title: Incident 1178: Google Gemini CLI reportedly deletes user files
summary: Records that the agent continued after a failed directory creation and its moves overwrote files.

title: OpenAI explains why ChatGPT became too sycophantic
summary: A model update was rolled back for being overly agreeable after over-weighting short-term user feedback.

title: Understanding Code Agent Behaviour: An Empirical Study of Success and Failure Trajectories
summary: Failed trajectories are longer and more variable; 72 to 81% of failures still found the right files.

title: Beyond Resolution Rates: Behavioral Drivers of Coding Agent Success and Failure
summary: 9,374 trajectories: the length-failure link vanishes when difficulty is controlled; context gathering and validation predict success.

title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
summary: Agents left assigned files unread in 67.9% of runs and misreported in 80.4% of those; false claimants missed planted defects about 1.8 times as often.

title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents
summary: False success claims are a large share of failures; LLM judges detect them poorly (AUROC at most 0.65); checking actual state works better.

title: How Coding Agents Fail Their Users: A Large-Scale Analysis of Developer-Agent Misalignment in 20,574 Real-World Sessions
summary: Seven recurring misalignment forms; 91.49% of resolutions needed explicit user correction; constraint violations and inaccurate self-reporting grow in share.

title: Evaluating LLM Agents on Automated Software Analysis Tasks
summary: Agents stop prematurely and self-validated success consistently overstates manually verified success.

title: Pricing
summary: Per-million-token prices for current models including the 100,000-token price step on the smallest tier; checked on the access date.

title: Models overview
summary: Model ids, positioning, context windows and headline prices for the current line-up.
